title: Two 25-degree spin tilts restore periapse libration in a tested rapid-rotation model of TYC 9179-1083-1
abstract: We let both stellar spin axes move in an averaged model of the published TYC 9179-1083-1 orbit. This tests a prior rapid-rotation example that forces the spins to stay aligned. With secondary spin period 0.12 day, apsidal constant 0.10, selected published radii and primary spin period 10 days, circulation survives spin backreaction near alignment. The inner eccentricity spans 0.158-0.546. At both tested spin azimuths, a 20-degree secondary tilt gives circulation and a 25-degree tilt gives libration over 6,000 years. At 90 degrees, eccentricity reaches 0.712. An adiabatic spin-average coefficient predicts an approximate transition at 23.54 degrees and explains the tilt trend. Two tighter integrations, torque balance and apsidal-rate checks support the implementation. This supplies a coupled spin tool and shows why a rotation period alone cannot establish the dynamical class. There are no new observations or spin measurements. Fixed stellar structure, leading averaged quadrupoles, one fitted orbit and no data refit limit the result. Code, fitted inputs, all 18 nominal trajectories, source hashes and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Coupled spin evolution at secondary rotation period 0.12 day. A 20-degree tilt circulates and a 25-degree tilt librates in the tested states. The spin average explains the trend. The orbit and stellar constants are fixed; no spin is measured.
